summary: Constraint conflict: disabling hibernation at system level affects battery operation, but this task requires AC-only changes with battery settings unchanged. Protocol Safety rule 2 requires refusal. No Windows settings were changed.
evidence: Reviewed task at origin/main f5fa1df2b60862a99db23976ffb05c4927e08e68; claim published as bfa9d66.
Objective: Disable hibernation at system level. Constraint: AC power settings only; leave battery settings unchanged.
Available power states: Standby (S0 Low Power Idle) Network Connected; Hibernate.
HIBERNATEIDLE query: Current AC Power Setting Index 0x00000000; Current DC Power Setting Index 0x00000000.
Microsoft documents hibernation disable as a computer-wide feature change: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-client/setup-upgrade-and-drivers/disable-and-re-enable-hibernation

Microsoft documents that a zero hibernate timeout can still use the adaptive threshold on Modern Standby systems: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/sleep-settings-hibernate-idle-timeout
notes: Rollback: none needed because no OS mutation occurred. Task 001 proved the requested timeout values were zero; that is not proof that every sleep path is disabled. A revised task limited to AC lid/power/sleep-button actions can be reviewed under existing approval. Global hibernation, screensaver, and lock-screen objectives should be separated from the AC-only constraint. No auto-login changes. No guarantee that software can suppress critical battery or thermal shutdown. The user-approved poll schedule remains two minutes; the revised protocol requests 30-second heartbeats, which this scheduler has not been configured to provide.
